text.p: Italian debt markets gave up a firmer start and followed U.S. Treasuries and the bund market lower by later afternoon while the lira's early strength soon ran out of steam, dealers said.
"It was an encouraging start, but the market could not hold at those levels especially after the lower tone to Treasuries," said one trader on the LIFFE market.

Dealers pointed out that the early strength in the market was prompted by the firmer trend to the lira, and when the Italian currency weakened BTP's lost their support and slipped lower in a largely featureless trading day.
Investors still have background worries over a delay in EMU and concerns over political difficulties over the passage of the 1997 mini-budget, with the bond market direction unclear.
"It's been a technical trading day with few influences except currency and other bonds markets," another trader on the LIFFE market added.
Dealers said that the BTP bond market looks set for more of this uncertain drifting trend awaiting fresh news on EMU or the mini-budget which faces a struggle to get through parliament.
